editorial:
Ever felt like you just couldn't face the real world after graduation? That is exactly where you find our main character in this breezy comedy. She is stuck in a sleepy southern college town, hiding out in an empty apartment and doing absolutely nothing with her life. Most of her time is spent hanging out with the building's maintenance man, who is just as laid back as she is. The whole vibe feels like a lazy Sunday afternoon where the only goal is to avoid doing any actual work. It captures that weird, floating feeling of being an adult but having no clue what you are actually doing.

You will love the chemistry between the two leads because their banter feels real and funny. While the plot is pretty slow and does not have any massive shocks, the dialogue keeps things moving. Some people might find the lack of a big plot frustrating, but it works if you just want to relax. If you want to see it, streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video is the way to go for those bright southern colors. You could also rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night with friends.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the main character finally gets a call for a real job, but she realizes she does not want to leave her lazy bubble. She has a heart-to-heart with the maintenance man and discovers he was actually a college professor who quit years ago. They both decide to stop hiding from life and move forward. She takes the job, but they promise to keep their friendship, ending the movie on a hopeful, happy note.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about finding yourself and lazy summer days.
